correctness.rationale: The graph has twenty vertices and thirty edges explicitly reconstructed as \(\operatorname{GP}(10,3)\). Complete perfect-matching DFS yields sixty facets, corroborated by an independently computed ten-by-ten bipartite permanent of sixty. A distinct enumeration of all 113,192 graph matchings using residual perfect-completion DP gives exactly 44,282 extendible faces including the empty face. A verified face matching pairs 22,124 nonempty Hasse covers and has critical cells one in dimension zero, thirty-one in dimension three, one in dimension four. A Kahn topological sort visits all 44,281 nonempty faces through 244,830 oriented Hasse incidences, proving acyclicity. A signed algebraic-Morse gradient reduction gives a 31-by-1 all-zero INTEGRAL boundary, not just mod-two evidence. The three-skeleton is a wedge of thirty-one 3-spheres; since \(\pi_3(\bigvee^{31}S^3)\cong\mathbb Z^{31}\) and is detected by degrees, the 4-cell attaches trivially, giving precisely the claimed integral homotopy equivalence. The actual standalone checker and its output are bundled. Independent mod-two boundary ranks confirm the corresponding Betti numbers.

originality.rationale: Against the inspected public papers, published records and recoverable accessible overlap claims, no covering theorem for the perfect-matching complex of the twenty-vertex Desargues graph was found. The same graph has a published classification of its larger ORDINARY matching complex, but a homotopy classification of a supercomplex does not determine that of an extendible-matching subcomplex. The nearest same-construction Heawood theorem concerns a different incidence graph and contains no all-cubic-graphs statement. The inspected original papers have honeycomb and polygonal-line hypotheses not satisfied by the Desargues graph. Absolute novelty against unindexed documents is not asserted.
residual_risks: The bibliography and index searches cannot exclude an unindexed or unpublished independent computation of the same perfect-matching homotopy type.
The proof has a finite but nontrivial computer-assisted signed Morse boundary certificate, supplied as independently runnable code; no third-party audit is claimed.

value.rationale: The graph is the canonical twenty-vertex Desargues incidence graph, equivalently the bipartite double cover of the Petersen graph, and its perfect-matching subcomplex is mathematically natural. The prior ordinary matching complex has homotopy in dimensions five and six, while the extendible matching subcomplex has a distinct integral mixed-dimensional wedge in dimensions three and four. Both the exact integer attaching map and full homotopy classification solve a natural finite topology problem not implied by neighboring calculations. No general theorem is needed for the value of this natural complete finite classification; no broader generalization is asserted.
